page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is a network-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 30.0 GB, allocating 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying processor incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX (tile and int8) as well as AVX-512 extensions. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU execution. The server achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2,256.0 alongside top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 15.25 GB/sec and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 35.04 GB/sec. Text processing workloads similarly achieve top-tier performance at 2,977.0 points. In contrast, multi-threaded throughput sits in the middle 50% across most workloads, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,502.0, a PassMark CPU score of 15,872.98, and static web serving throughput of 16.99 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 61.57 GB/sec, while write operations reach 36.0 GB/sec.

On lightweight artificial intelligence inference tasks, the instance performs well using its vector extensions, recording a top-tier text generation rate of 352.64 tokens/sec on a 135M model. However, throughput drops significantly when scaling model size without dedicated acceleration, achieving a weak 7.21 tokens/sec on a 7B parameter model. In-memory data store performance is consistent with its resource tier, delivering 12.12 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given its balanced CPU-to-memory allocation and high per-core single-thread efficiency, Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 serves standard application tiers, web serving, software compilation pipelines, and entry-level batch processing. Workloads requiring massive multi-core concurrency, high-parameter machine learning generation, or ultra-low-latency local disk I/O may require larger instances or specialized hardware accelerators.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is a network-optimized server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 30.0 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture with a large 260 MB L3 cache, the system features hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The instance carries no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote persistent storage. Benchmark data reflects top-tier single-core compute performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,256.0, fast single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.25 GB/sec, and high text processing throughput. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth (61.57 GB/sec read), and Redis execution (12.12 million ops/sec) remain in the middle tier. c4n-standard-8 is well suited for web applications, build runners, and general-purpose business computing where single-threaded responsiveness and standard memory density are prioritized over massive parallel acceleration.
